title: Continuous integration: triggers, jobs and matrix runs

videos.script: Lessons 1 to 4 ran the tests on a laptop. That works until somebody forgets to. {{laptop}} Continuous integration is the habit of merging often, with a machine that checks every merge. It checks it from a clean start, not from your laptop's files. {{definition}} This lesson builds the smallest CI there is, a git hook of fifty lines, so you can see the whole loop at once. Push, check out, run, report. {{loop}} Then it catches two real mistakes. A test whose data file was never committed. It passes on the laptop and fails everywhere else. {{untracked}} And a change to the dispatch rule. It passes in São Paulo and fails on every machine set to UTC. {{matrix}} You will read the failure from the shape of the matrix before opening a single log. {{shape}} The rest is what makes a pipeline worth trusting. Exit codes that do not lie. Caches with honest keys. Flaky tests found and fixed, not retried. And a run short enough that people wait for it. {{trust}}
